R696.note: jwt.verify with a pinned HS256 algorithm list closes the unsigned-decode path; the new startup check on JWT_SECRET and the 401-on-bad-token path are stated and do not block a legitimate admin token.

R697.note: The env-array injection is closed by dropping argsEnv, but the fix repurposes param into a command argument it was never passed as, behind an allowlist that still permits a leading '-' and '../' (option/path injection surface) and rejects header values the original accepted.

R698.note: processEntities:false in fast-xml-parser closes XXE, but the XPath '//order/id' (descendant anywhere) becomes root-only 'doc.order?.id', so an order nested under any wrapper element now 400s, and an empty <id> flips from 200 to 400 - neither is mentioned.

R699.note: Re-indexing tasks[activeIndex] after the push_back removes the dangling reference with identical semantics; nothing else observable changes.

R700.note: SigningMethodHMAC assertion in keyFunc plus WithValidMethods pins the algorithm server-side; algorithm pinning is the fix itself and a legitimately signed HS256 token still passes.

R701.note: in_array strict check rejects before require() and keeps 'summary' as default as the contract requires; the three-name list is guessed rather than derived from the plugins directory, which is a residual risk but is the allowlist the contract calls for.

R702.note: Moving the deletion to POST behind protection.Handler closes it since CrossOriginProtection ignores GET; the GET route becoming a same-origin confirmation form is stated plainly and email links still work.

R703.note: Path.resolve() follows the symlink before is_relative_to() checks containment, closing the escape; nested paths still open, missing paths still raise FileNotFoundError, and the controller's download_name is untouched.

R704.note: 'sh -c' is kept, so the split argument becomes $0 of the shell rather than an argument to echo - injection is closed on POSIX only by accident and the value is never echoed; on the Windows branch cmd.exe /c re-parses the joined command line, where Java does not quote '&' or '|', so that path stays injectable, and the write-up asserts the opposite behaviour.

R705.note: Per-stream setObjectInputFilter before readObject keeps the native wire format and blocks gadget classes; RuntimeException still surfaces on rejection, and the caveat about OrderEvent fields outside java.base is stated (though the java.util example given is itself in java.base).

R706.note: AES/GCM/NoPadding with a fresh SecureRandom 96-bit IV replaces the ECB default; the IV||ciphertext||tag layout is a ciphertext-format change but is unavoidable off ECB, is stated explicitly, and the 400-on-missing-ssn and Base64 text/plain response are preserved.

R707.note: Rejecting when bytesRead < 8 stops the zero-padded header from being compared, closing the unchecked-read path; ReadExactly or a fill loop would be the sturdier shape, but no real PNG or PDF upload is turned away and the change is minimal.

R708.note: The four filter metacharacters are escaped correctly so injection is closed, but the switch maps the space character to backslash-00 (the NUL escape) - the write-up describes this case as 'NULL character', so any legitimate uid containing a space is silently rewritten with an embedded NUL octet and stops matching.
